subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements about a fort:

1. It was originally known as Mankal.

2. It was built on a hilltop in the year 1143.

In above mentioned sentences, forts is being talked about?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Golconda Fort**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **​Golconda Fort** is a **historic fortress** and ruined city.
 
• It is situated in** Hyderabad, Telangana,** India, in the **western outskirts.**
 
• **Mankal **was its original name.
 
• The fort was initially constructed in the **11th century** using** mud walls** by **Kakatiya monarch Prataparudra.**
 
• It was built on a **hilltop** in the **year 1143.**
 
• **Deo Rai, Rajah of Warangal**, gave it to the** Bahmani Monarchs** during Sultan Muhammad Shah's rule of the **Bahmani Sultanate (1358–1375 A.D.).**
 
• In **2014, UNESCO** added the complex to its** "tentative list" **of potential **World Heritage Sites.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chitradurg Fort:**

 
 
• In the** Chitradurga District of Karnataka,** India, the Chitradurg Fort is a **stronghold.**
 
• The region's dynastic rulers, including the** Chalukyas and Hoysalas, **constructed the fort in phases between the **11th and 13th centuries.**
 
• Later, it was constructed by the **Chitradurga Nayakas** of the** Vijayanagar Empire.​**
 
 
 
• **Daulatabad Fort:**
 
 
• At** Daulatabad village, Maharashtra, India**, close to Aurangabad, there is an ancient **defensive citadel** called Daulatabad Fort.
 
• The first Yadava ruler**, Bhillama V**, constructed the city's renowned triangle stronghold in about **1187.**
 
 
 
• **Fort Aguada:**
 
 
• In **Goa**, India, there is a well-preserved **Portuguese fort** from the seventeenth century called Fort Aguada.
 
• The fort was initially built in **1612** as a** defense against the Dutch. **
